model.title: Model
model.subtitle: qwen3_next
model.doc: The model's width, vocabulary, residual algebra and initialization: the settings every layer reads.

fields.doc: The width of the residual stream.
The vocabulary's size: the embedding's rows and the head's outputs.
The residual algebra: what `[f]` means. none is x + f(x).
How weight matrices start.

node:n.0.title: Token embedding
node:n.0.subtitle: embed
node:n.0.doc:
The token embedding: token ids to the stream, by a table of `vocab_size` rows
of `d_model`. A model starts with one, and a tied head and nextn read the table
of its first. Under a residual algebra that widens the stream, it returns that
many copies of the embedding.

fields.doc: Learned absolute positions (GPT-2): a table of this many, added to the embedding; None: none.
Multiply the embedding by sqrt(d_model) (Gemma).
A norm of the embedding, after the scale and before positions are added (Inkling); nextn reads the embedding normalized too.
Dropout rate of the embedding, in training.

node:n.1.title: Repeat
node:n.1.subtitle: ×12
node:n.1.doc: `body^n`: n copies of the body in sequence, each with its own parameters.

fields.doc: How many fresh copies of the body run in sequence.

node:n.1.0.0.0.0.0.title: RMSNorm
node:n.1.0.0.0.0.0.subtitle: rmsnorm · norm
node:n.1.0.0.0.0.0.doc:
Layer normalization (Ba et al., 2016) or RMSNorm (Zhang & Sennrich, 2019).

``layernorm`` subtracts the mean over the width and divides by the standard
deviation; ``rmsnorm`` only divides by the root mean square. Then each multiplies
by a learned gain per channel (`affine`) and adds a learned bias (`bias`). A norm
is a layer, ``[norm attn]``, and a setting of layers that normalize something of
their own, as ``gqa(qk_norm=rmsnorm)``.

fields.doc: Added to the variance (rmsnorm: mean square) before its root.
A learned gain per channel, the norm's scale.
A learned bias per channel, added last (GPT-2's layernorms).
The gain as 1 + w, with w learned from 0 (Gemma, Qwen3-Next).
Where the gain starts: 1 / sqrt(layers) is Trinity's depth-scaled sandwich norm, [norm attn norm(gain_init=layers ^ -0.5)].
Multiply by the gain before normalizing, norm(w * x), not after (Muse Spark).

node:n.1.0.0.0.0.1.title: Gated DeltaNet
node:n.1.0.0.0.0.1.subtitle: gdn · delta
node:n.1.0.0.0.0.1.doc:
Gated DeltaNet: the delta rule with a scalar per-head decay (Yang et al., 2025).

DeltaNet whose state decays by ``exp(g)`` before each token's update, with
``g = -exp(A_log) softplus(W_a x + dt_bias)`` per value head, as in Qwen3-Next:
``gdn(num_heads=16, num_v_heads=32, head_dim=128)``.

fields.doc: Query and key heads.
Width of a query and a key head: the state's rows.
Value heads. With more of them than q/k heads, each q/k head serves a group of them (Qwen3-Next). None -> num_heads
Width of a value head: the state's columns. None -> head_dim
Causal depthwise conv on q, k and v, of this many taps, each then SiLU'd; None disables it.
Activation of a gate on the output, after its norm and before the output projection; None disables it.
Epsilon of the output norm (Qwen3-Next: 1e-6; Kimi Linear and fla: 1e-5).

node:n.1.0.0.1.0.1.title: Mixture of experts
node:n.1.0.0.1.0.1.subtitle: moe · experts
node:n.1.0.0.1.0.1.doc:
Token-choice top-k mixture of experts (Mixtral, DeepSeekMoE, Qwen3-MoE).

A router scores the `num_experts` routed experts for every token, and the token
goes through its `top_k` best, their outputs summed by the router's weights; the
shared experts, if any, take every token. A loss, a bias or both balance the
experts' loads (`load_balancing`). The run's ``methods.moe`` says how the experts
run: every expert on every token (``dense``), each on its own tokens
(``sorted``, the default), or over devices by expert parallelism.

fields.doc: Routed experts.
Routed experts each token goes through.
Each routed expert: its type, intermediate_size and activation, its limit, up_softcap and up_offset, and its biases. Routed experts have no dropout.
Hidden units: the output width of up (and of gate).

fields.type: relu | relu2 | gelu | gelu_tanh | swish | sigmoid | tanh | softplus | situ | quick_gelu
fields.doc: Of the hidden units, or of the gate when gated.
Dropout rate of the output, in training.
Biases on the up, gate and down projections.
Clamped SwiGLU: the gate input is capped at limit, the up branch at +-limit (gpt-oss, DeepSeek-V4); None: no clamp.
Soft-capping of the up branch, cap * tanh(up / cap) (Kimi K3); None: none.
Added to a gated MLP's up branch after it is clipped: gpt-oss's up + 1.
Experts every token goes through, run as one MLP of num_shared_experts times the shared expert's intermediate_size.
A shared expert; None -> like `expert`.
A sigmoid gate on the shared experts' output, from the token (Qwen).
How the router scores the experts from its logits: by a softmax over them, a sigmoid each (DeepSeek-V3), or sqrt(softplus(logit)) each (DeepSeek-V4).
A learned bias on the router's logits (gpt-oss), unlike aux_free's on the choice.
Multiplies the logits before scoring (Muse Spark)

For benchmarks: a training forward routes by random logits, N(0, 1), so that each expert takes an even share of the picks in expectation and a capacity drops few; their gradient goes to the router's own logits (Megatron-Core's moe_router_force_load_balancing).
Divide the top-k scores by their sum, so the weights sum to 1; else the weights are the scores.
Multiplies the weights (DeepSeek-V3: 2.5).
Group-limited routing: pick top_k_groups of num_groups first (DeepSeek-V3). Each group is scored by the sum of its best two experts' scores.
Groups each token picks its experts from.

Load balancing by a loss, a bias or both. aux_free adds a bias per expert to the scores that pick the top-k, not to the weights. Every training step moves it by bias_update_rate: up for experts picked less than the mean, down for those picked more (DeepSeek-V3). smebu moves the same bias by a step that shrinks as an expert's load nears the mean: tanh(bias_softclamp * (mean - load) / mean) times the rate, centered over the experts and averaged by a momentum of bias_momentum (Trinity).
How far the bias moves each training step, for each expert: aux_free's step, and SMEBU's largest (Trinity Large: 5e-4).
aux_free: subtract the bias's mean after every move, so that the biases stay centered (Trinity Nano and Mini). SMEBU always centers its moves.
SMEBU's kappa: how soon tanh saturates, a load off the mean by 1 / kappa of it moving the bias by 0.76 of the rate.
SMEBU's beta: the decay of the moves' running average, which moves the bias.

Weight of each layer's balance loss, E * sum_e f_e P_e, where f_e is the fraction of top-k picks that go to expert e and P_e its mean score, normalized over the experts (Switch; DeepSeek-V3, eqs. 17-20). None -> 1e-2, or 0 with a bias. Every layer adds its own, as in Megatron-LM. transformers pools the layers into one loss and counts tokens, not picks, so its coefficient c is about c * top_k / layers.
Over the whole batch (Switch, Qwen), or per sequence and then averaged (the complementary sequence-wise loss of DeepSeek-V3).
LatentMoE: routed experts run in a narrower space of this width, between a down and an up projection; the router and the shared experts see the full width (Nemotron 3). None: the full width.
LatentMoE's norm of the tokens after the down projection; None: none.
A norm of the routed sum (Kimi K3), before LatentMoE's up projection; None: none.
Of each routed expert's output.
The shared experts are weighted by the router too, normalized with the top-k (Inkling); otherwise they are added with weight 1.

node:n.1.0.3.0.0.1.title: Grouped-query attention
node:n.1.0.3.0.0.1.subtitle: gqa · attn
node:n.1.0.3.0.0.1.doc:
Grouped-query attention; MHA when num_kv_heads == num_heads, MQA when it is 1.

Causal softmax attention (Vaswani et al., 2017) of `num_heads` query heads and
`num_kv_heads` key and value heads, each shared by a group of
``num_heads / num_kv_heads`` query heads (Ainslie et al., 2023):
``gqa(num_heads=32, num_kv_heads=8, rope=rope())``.

Ports: ``v`` exports the value heads, or imports them for value-residual mixing
(ResFormer); ``kv`` exports keys and values, or imports them instead of computing
its own (cross-layer KV sharing, YOCO / CLA); ``index`` shares the indexer's top-k.

node:n.1.0.3.1.0.1.title: Mixture of experts
node:n.1.0.3.1.0.1.subtitle: moe · experts
node:n.1.0.3.1.0.1.doc:

A router scores the `num_experts` routed experts for every token, and the token
goes through its `top_k` best, their outputs summed by the router's weights; the
shared experts, if any, take every token. A loss, a bias or both balance the
experts' loads (`load_balancing`). The run's ``methods.moe`` says how the experts
run: every expert on every token (``dense``), each on its own tokens
(``sorted``, the default), or over devices by expert parallelism.

Hidden units: the output width of up (and of gate).

A shared expert; None -> like `expert`.

node:n.5.1.title: Next-token embedding
node:n.5.1.subtitle: nextn
node:n.5.1.doc:
Multi-token prediction input (DeepSeek-V3): ``h -> W [norm(e_{i+k}); norm(h)]``.
For the k-th nextn in a forward pass, ``e_{i+k}`` is `embed`'s output for the
token k positions ahead (scaled and normalized, without positions). So every head
after it predicts one token further ahead, and a shared MTP module run twice
looks 1, then 2 tokens ahead (Nemotron 3, GLM-5). An MTP module is
``$h! nextn block norm @h head``, run after the main head.

On a widened stream it mixes the embedding into each copy, ``W_e norm(e) + W_h
norm(R)_j``, normalizing the copies together (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). On one stream
under a widening algebra it widens its output, as `embed` does.
